case_number: Criminal Appeal No(s). 200 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP(Crl.) No(s). 8283 of 2021)
summary: The appellant, Shafiya Khan, challenged the High Court's refusal to quash criminal proceedings under Sections 494, 420, 504, 506, 467, 468, and 471 IPC, filed by her brother-in-law alleging bigamy and forgery in her second marriage after her first marriage was voided. The appellant claimed her first marriage was annulled by panchayat in 2014 due to non-consummation and minority, and her second marriage was valid under Sharia law in 2016. She argued the charges were malicious, with no prima facie evidence, and constituted an abuse of legal process. The Supreme Court examined the allegations under the test laid down in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, assessing whether the FIR disclosed cognizable offences or was manifestly mala fide.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 3 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006
Article 226 of the Constitution of India
State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed and the criminal proceedings against the appellant were quashed on the ground that they amounted to an abuse of process and lacked prima facie evidence for the offences charged.
